files..gitlab-ci.yml:
spec:
  inputs:
    tag_release_image_version:
      type: "string"
      default: "latest"
      description: "tag for the image used to create new project releases"
    release_schedule:
      type: boolean
      default: false
      description: "toggle release jobs on/off; set by pipeline schedules only!"
---
variables:
  GO_VERSION: "1.27.0"
  GITLAB_ADVANCED_SAST_ENABLED: "true"
  # glab image version for the weekly tag-release job. Defaults to latest
  # (dogfooding); override on the release schedule to pin a known-good version
  # if a :latest regression ever breaks the release, without a new commit.
  TAG_RELEASE_IMAGE_VERSION: $[[ inputs.tag_release_image_version ]]
  RELEASE_SCHEDULE: $[[ inputs.release_schedule ]]

.code-patterns: &code-patterns
  - ".gitlab/**/*"
  - "**/*.go"
  - "scripts/**/*"
  - "test/**/*"
  - ".gitignore"
  - ".gitlab-ci.yml"
  - ".golangci.yml"
  - "Makefile"
  - "go.mod"
  - "go.sum"

.sign_windows_base:
  image: ${CI_REGISTRY}/gitlab-com/gl-infra/common-ci-tasks-images/code-signer:1.3.0
  extends: .google-oidc:auth
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG && $CI_SERVER_HOST == "gitlab.com" && ($CI_PROJECT_PATH == "gitlab-org/cli" || $CI_PROJECT_PATH == "gitlab-org/security/cli")
  stage: release
  artifacts:
    expire_in: 7 days
  variables:
    GCLOUD_PROJECT: gitlab-ci-runners-signing
    SERVICE_ACCOUNT: gitlab-cli-signer@gitlab-ci-runners-signing.iam.gserviceaccount.com
    WI_POOL_PROVIDER: //iam.googleapis.com/projects/8522242139/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/gitlab-pool-oidc-$CI_PROJECT_ID/providers/gitlab-jwt-$CI_PROJECT_ID

.use_signed_if_available: &use_signed_if_available
  - |
    if [ -d "signed/" ]; then
      echo "Using signed binaries"
      rm -rf bin/
      mv signed bin
      ls -al bin
    else
      echo "Using unsigned binaries"
    fi

# run the pipeline only on MRs, tags, default branch, and the release schedule
workflow:
  auto_cancel:
    # `conservative`, the default, refuses to cancel a superseded pipeline once
    # any job with `interruptible: false` has started, and the policy-injected
    # dependency-scanning job starts immediately and is not ours to mark. That
    # left superseded pipelines running their whole build stage. `interruptible`
    # cancels the jobs we did mark and lets the rest finish.
    on_new_commit: interruptible
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

# Skip jobs in the weekly release schedule, this intentionally does not match other scheduled pipelines
.skip-on-release-schedule: &skip-on-release-schedule
  if: $RELEASE_SCHEDULE == "true"
  when: never

default:
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}golang:${GO_VERSION}
  tags:
    # NOTE: largest linux-based hosted runner available in Free tier.
    # see https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/hosted_runners/linux/#machine-types-available-for-linux---x86-64
    - "saas-linux-medium-amd64"
  retry:
    max: 2
    when:
      - runner_external_dependency_failure

# Stage order here is presentation, not sequencing: every job declares its own
# `needs:`, so these are lanes in the pipeline graph rather than gates. The one
# exception is the dependency-scanning job injected by a group security policy,
# whose `needs:` we do not control. Declaring its stage (the policy fixes the
# name) keeps it from being appended after everything else, where it was the
# last job to finish in every pipeline.
stages:
  - application-security-testing
  - checks
  - documentation
  - test
  - build
  - review
  - release

include:
  - template: Jobs/SAST.gitlab-ci.yml
  # No Dependency-Scanning template: it provides the Gemnasium analyzer, which
  # is deprecated as of GitLab 17.9, and a group security policy already
  # injects the SBOM-based analyzer that replaces it. Including both ran two
  # dependency scans per pipeline.
  - template: Jobs/Secret-Detection.gitlab-ci.yml
  - project: "gitlab-com/gl-security/security-operations/infrastructure-security-public/oidc-modules"
    ref: 3.4.0
    file: templates/gcp_auth.yaml

# From: https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/caching/#cache-go-dependencies
# Base template for Go caching - extended by jobs that need Go dependencies
.go-cache:
  variables:
    GOPATH: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.go
    GOCACHE: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.gocache
    GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.golangci-lint-cache
  cache:
    paths:
      - $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.go/pkg/mod/
      - $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.gocache/
      - $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.golangci-lint-cache/
    # Keyed per job rather than on go.sum. Go's module and build caches are
    # content-addressed, so an entry that no longer matches is ignored rather
    # than used wrongly, whereas a go.sum-keyed cache went fully cold on every
    # dependency bump - one every day or two here, costing tests:unit 153s ->
    # 682s and lint 79s -> 309s whenever a pipeline landed on a new key.
    key: "go-$CI_JOB_NAME_SLUG"
    policy: pull-push

.documentation:
  stage: documentation
  interruptible: true
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
  needs: []
  dependencies: []

.test:
  stage: test
  interruptible: true
  rules:
    - *skip-on-release-schedule
    - changes: *code-patterns
      when: always
  # None of these jobs consume another job's output, so none should wait for a
  # stage boundary. Without this they queued behind the documentation stage.
  needs: []

check_docs_update:
  extends:
    - .documentation
    - .go-cache
  script:
    - make gen-docs
    - |-
      git status
      if [[ $(git add -A --dry-run) ]]; then
        echo '✖ ERROR: Documentation changes detected!';
        git diff --color --ws-error-highlight=all
        echo '✖ These changes require a documentation update. Run `make gen-docs` to regenerate the docs and navigation, then commit. See https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/tree/main/docs#generating-the-docs.';
        exit 1;
      else
        echo '✔ No documentation updates detected.';
        exit 0;
      fi

check_docs_markdown:
  image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com/lint-markdown:alpine-3.24-vale-3.21.0-markdownlint2-0.23.2-lychee-0.24.2-rumdl-0.2.69
  extends: .documentation
  script:
    # Lint prose
    - vale --minAlertLevel error docs
    # Lint Markdown
    - markdownlint-cli2 'docs/**/*.md' *.md
    # Check links
    - lychee --offline --include-fragments docs/**/*.md *.md

docs hugo_build:
  image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com/docs-gitlab-com-builder:hugo-0.154.5
  extends: .documentation
  variables:
    DOCS_BRANCH: "main"
  before_script:
    # Check if this a release branch, which would be the case for a backport.
    # If this is a backport MR, we need to checkout the appropriate version
    # of the Docs website.
    - |
      if [[ $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME =~ [0-9]+-[0-9]+-stable ]]; then
        BRANCH_NAME=$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME
        echo "Detected merge request to stable branch: $BRANCH_NAME"
      # Check if we're directly on a stable branch (direct push/commit)
      elif [[ $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH =~ [0-9]+-[0-9]+-stable ]]; then
        BRANCH_NAME=$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH
        echo "Detected direct commit to stable branch: $BRANCH_NAME"
      fi

      # Extract version info if we found a stable branch
      if [[ -n $BRANCH_NAME ]]; then
        MAJOR=$(echo $BRANCH_NAME | cut -d '-' -f 1)
        MINOR=$(echo $BRANCH_NAME | cut -d '-' -f 2)
        # Convert GitLab style (17-9-stable-ee) to Docs style (17.9)
        DOCS_BRANCH_CANDIDATE="$MAJOR.$MINOR"

        # Check if the branch exists in the Docs website repo, fallback to main if not
        if git ls-remote --heads --exit-code https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com.git "refs/heads/$DOCS_BRANCH_CANDIDATE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          DOCS_BRANCH="$DOCS_BRANCH_CANDIDATE"
          echo "Using docs-gitlab-com branch $DOCS_BRANCH for release branch"
        else
          DOCS_BRANCH="main"
          echo "Branch $DOCS_BRANCH_CANDIDATE does not exist, falling back to main"
        fi
      fi
    # Clone the Docs website project
    - git clone --depth 1 --filter=tree:0 --branch $DOCS_BRANCH https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com.git
    - cd docs-gitlab-com
    - make add-latest-icons
  script:
    # Remove unwanted files from CLI docs/ to avoid conflicts with docs/source/
    # See https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com/-/merge_requests/1554#note_2901887344
    - rm -f ../docs/index.rst ../docs/*.md
    # Test that Hugo will build
    - hugo --gc --printPathWarnings --panicOnWarning  --environment test
    # Test for invalid index pages
    # See https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com/-/blob/main/scripts/check-index-filenames.sh
    - make check-index-pages SEARCH_DIR="../docs/source"
    #- make check-index-pages SEARCH_DIR="../doc-locale/source" # Enable when translation is added

.review-docs:
  image: ruby:3.4-alpine3.23
  extends: .documentation
  stage: review
  # Overrides .documentation: cancelling these mid-run would leave the docs
  # review environment in an inconsistent state.
  interruptible: false
  cache: {}
  dependencies: []
  before_script:
    - gem install gitlab --no-doc
    # We need to download the script rather than clone the repo since the
    # review-docs-cleanup job will not be able to run when the branch gets
    # deleted (when merging the MR).
    - apk add --update openssl
    - wget https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/master/scripts/trigger-build.rb
    - chmod 755 trigger-build.rb
  variables:
    GIT_STRATEGY: none
    DOCS_GITLAB_REPO_SUFFIX: cli
    # By default, deploy the Review App using the `main` branch of the `gitlab-org/gitlab-docs` project
    DOCS_BRANCH: main
  when: manual

# Trigger a docs build in docs-gitlab-com project
# Useful to preview the docs changes live
# https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/review_apps/
review-docs-deploy:
  extends:
    - .review-docs
  environment:
    name: review/mr-${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID}
    url: https://docs.gitlab.com/upstream-review-mr-${DOCS_GITLAB_REPO_SUFFIX}-${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID}/${DOCS_GITLAB_REPO_SUFFIX}
    auto_stop_in: 2 weeks
    on_stop: review-docs-cleanup
  script:
    - ./trigger-build.rb docs deploy

# Cleanup remote environment of docs-gitlab-com
review-docs-cleanup:
  extends:
    - .review-docs
  environment:
    name: review/mr-${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID}
    action: stop
  script:
    - ./trigger-build.rb docs cleanup

check_go_generated_code:
  extends:
    - .go-cache
    - .test
  stage: checks
  script:
    - make generate
    - |
      echo "Checking git status"
      [ -z "$(git status --short)" ] || {
        echo "Error: Files should have been generated:";
        git status --short; echo "Diff:";
        git --no-pager diff HEAD;
        echo "Run \"make generate\" and try again";
        exit 1;
      }

lint_commit:
  stage: checks
  needs: []
  interruptible: true
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}node:24-slim
  script:
    - apt-get update && apt-get install -y git
    - git fetch origin $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME $CI_COMMIT_SHA
    - cd scripts/commit-lint && npm ci
    - ./lint.sh
  rules:
    - if: '$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID && $CI_PROJECT_VISIBILITY == "public"' # lint.js script makes an API call without authentication
      when: always

check_go_version:
  stage: checks
  needs: []
  interruptible: true
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}alpine:3
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache bash
  script:
    - scripts/check-go-version.sh
  rules:
    - *skip-on-release-schedule
    - changes:
        - go.mod
        - .tool-versions
        - .gitlab-ci.yml

check_embed:
  stage: checks
  needs: []
  interruptible: true
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}alpine:3
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache make
  script:
    - make check-embed

check_args:
  stage: checks
  needs: []
  interruptible: true
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}alpine:3
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache make
  script:
    - make check-args

# Lefthook runs these too, but it can be skipped with LEFTHOOK=0, so the
# enforcement point is here. The overlap gate blocks; the ratio is a number
# for the author to weigh and never fails the job.
lint:comments:
  extends:
    - .go-cache
    - .test
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}golang:${GO_VERSION}
  script:
    - go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0 ./cmd/... ./internal/...
    - |
      if [ -n "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA" ]; then
        git fetch --quiet origin "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA"
        go run ./scripts/comment-ratio -base "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA"
      fi

# Reachability scanning, which the other security jobs do not do: this fails
# only when our code has a call path into a vulnerable function, not merely
# when a vulnerable version is somewhere in the module graph.
#
# Blocking on the default branch and manual on merge requests. The result
# depends on the vulnerability database as much as on the code, so a new
# upstream advisory can turn it red with no change on our side. That belongs to
# whoever owns the default branch, not to whichever author pushed next. Anyone
# can still run it on their own merge request from the pipeline view. Modelled
# on the `vulnerability` job in gitlab-org/gitaly.
govulncheck:
  extends: .go-cache
  stage: application-security-testing
  needs: []
  interruptible: true
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}golang:${GO_VERSION}
  variables:
    # Pinned rather than @latest so a scanner release cannot change the
    # pipeline's verdict on its own. Renovate does not manage this.
    GOVULNCHECK_VERSION: "v1.8.0"
  rules:
    - *skip-on-release-schedule
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: manual
      allow_failure: true
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
  script:
    # Invoked by path: .go-cache points GOPATH at the project directory so the
    # cache can pick it up, and $GOPATH/bin is not on PATH in this image.
    - go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@${GOVULNCHECK_VERSION}
    # Built rather than `go run`, which collapses every non-zero status to 1
    # and would erase the difference between findings and a broken scanner.
    - go build -o bin/govulncheck-to-gitlab ./scripts/govulncheck-to-gitlab
    - $GOPATH/bin/govulncheck -format json ./... > govulncheck.json
    - ./bin/govulncheck-to-gitlab < govulncheck.json > gl-dependency-scanning-report.json
  artifacts:
    when: always
    access: "developer"
    expire_in: 7 days
    paths:
      - govulncheck.json
    reports:
      dependency_scanning: gl-dependency-scanning-report.json

lint:
  extends:
    - .go-cache
    - .test
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}golangci/golangci-lint:v2.13.1-alpine
  script:
    # Write the code coverage report to gl-code-quality-report.json
    # and print linting issues to stdout in the format: path/to/file:line description
    # add `--issues-exit-code 0` to ignore linting issues
    - golangci-lint run --output.text.path=stdout --output.text.colors=false --output.text.print-issued-lines=false --output.code-climate.path=gl-code-quality-report.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: gl-code-quality-report.json
    paths:
      - gl-code-quality-report.json
    expire_in: 7 days

tests:unit:
  extends:
    - .go-cache
    - .test
  # We currently only test on the latest version of Go which we also build against.
  # If we need to introduce testing for future versions of compatibility reasons
  # uncomment the below lines and adjust the `GO_VERSION` to included versions to test.
  # parallel:
  # matrix:
  # - GO_VERSION: ["1.22.3"]
  variables:
    # NOTE: required for race detector
    CGO_ENABLED: "1"
  script:
    - make test-race
  after_script:
    - echo -e "\e[0Ksection_start:`date +%s`:coverage[collapsed=true]\r\e[0KRunning coverage report"
    - make coverage
    - echo -e "\e[0Ksection_end:`date +%s`:coverage\r\e[0K"
  coverage: /^total:\t+\(statements\)\t+\d+\.\d+%$/
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      junit: coverage.xml
    access: "developer"
    expire_in: 7 days

tests:integration:
  extends:
    - .go-cache
    - .test
  # We currently only test on the latest version of Go which we also build against.
  # If we need to introduce testing for future versions of compatibility reasons
  # uncomment the below lines and adjust the `GO_VERSION` to included versions to test.
  # parallel:
  # matrix:
  # - GO_VERSION: ["1.22.3"]
  variables:
    # NOTE: required for race detector
    CGO_ENABLED: "1"
  script:
    # `goreleaser` also uses GITLAB_TOKEN and so we need to distinguish between
    # the GITLAB_TOKEN_TEST with less privilege used for testing and the GITLAB_TOKEN_RELEASE token
    # GITLAB_TEST_HOST is the GitLab instance used for the integration tests
    - GITLAB_TOKEN_TEST=$GITLAB_TOKEN_TEST GITLAB_TEST_HOST=$GITLAB_TEST_HOST make integration-test-race
  after_script:
    - echo -e "\e[0Ksection_start:`date +%s`:coverage[collapsed=true]\r\e[0KRunning coverage report"
    - make coverage
    - echo -e "\e[0Ksection_end:`date +%s`:coverage\r\e[0K"

.release:
  extends: .sign_windows_base
  tags:
    # NOTE: we really benefit from the capacities of this 2xlarge runner.
    # we only want to build from the canonical project so we don't really
    # need to bother about this being compatible with forks.
    - "saas-linux-2xlarge-amd64"
  stage: release
  image: ${GITLAB_DEPENDENCY_PROXY}docker:stable
  services:
    - name: docker:28-dind
      command: ["--mtu=1360"]
  variables:
    # Disable shallow cloning so that goreleaser can diff between tags to
    # generate a changelog.
    GIT_DEPTH: 0
  needs: [sign_windows_installer]
  dependencies: [sign_windows_installer]
  before_script:
    - !reference [.google-oidc:auth, before_script]
    - *use_signed_if_available
    # The OIDC module creates secrets in /var/run/secrets/gitlab, but this
    # mount is only available on the job container, not the docker:dind
    # service. Copy these files into the project dir to ensure
    # all containers can access it.
    - cp -r /var/run/secrets/gitlab .gitlab-secrets
  after_script:
    - !reference [.google-oidc:auth, after_script]
    - rm -rf .gitlab-secrets

build_test:
  extends: .release
  stage: build
  # Set here rather than on .release, which `release` also extends: a snapshot
  # build publishes nothing and is safe to cancel, an actual release is not.
  interruptible: true
  rules:
    - *skip-on-release-schedule
    - if: $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_EVENT_TYPE == "merge_train"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
      when: never
    - changes:
        - .goreleaser.yml
        - .gitlab-ci.yml
  script: |
    docker run --rm --privileged \
      -e CI=$CI \
      -e CI_COMMIT_TAG=$CI_COMMIT_TAG \
      -e APPSTORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_FILE=$APPSTORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_FILE \
      -e GCLOUD_PROJECT=$GCLOUD_PROJECT \
      -e GO_VERSION="$GO_VERSION" \
      -e GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS \
      -e HOST_PWD=$PWD \
      -v $PWD:/go/src/gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli \
      -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
      -w /go/src/gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli \
      goreleaser/goreleaser:nightly release --skip=sign --snapshot
  artifacts:
    name: goreleaser-artifacts
    paths:
      - dist/
    expire_in: 7 days
  # tests:unit gates here rather than further up the chain: this is the only
  # job in it expensive enough to be worth not running speculatively, at ~5
  # minutes on a 2xlarge. Optional because tag pipelines do not run tests:unit;
  # artifacts:false because only the signed installer is consumed.
  needs:
    - job: windows_installer
      optional: false
    - job: sign_windows_installer
      optional: true
    - job: tests:unit
      optional: true
      artifacts: false

# Weekly release: create the next tag, which triggers the tag-driven release
# pipeline below. See docs/release_process.md.
tag-release:
  stage: release
  image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:$TAG_RELEASE_IMAGE_VERSION
  needs: []
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: 0
    GITLAB_HOST: $CI_SERVER_HOST
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $RELEASE_SCHEDULE == "true"
  before_script:
    # glab image is Alpine without bash; the script needs it for set -o pipefail.
    - apk add --no-cache bash
  script:
    # Assign the release token inline, not via `variables:` above: the
    # project-level GITLAB_TOKEN CI/CD variable outranks job variables, so
    # setting GITLAB_TOKEN here is the only way glab uses the release token
    # (must NOT be CI_JOB_TOKEN, whose tags don't trigger the release pipeline).
    # Matches notify-issues-on-release.
    - GITLAB_TOKEN="$GITLAB_TOKEN_RELEASE" scripts/release/create-release-tag.sh

release:
  extends: .release
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
  script: |
    docker run --rm --privileged \
      -e CI=$CI \
      -e CI_COMMIT_TAG=$CI_COMMIT_TAG \
      -e APPSTORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_FILE=$APPSTORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_FILE \
      -e GCLOUD_PROJECT=$GCLOUD_PROJECT \

# .gitlab/duo/agent-config.yml
#
# Configures the CI/CD environment for GitLab Duo coding agent flows.
# Mirrors the project's standard development setup using mise to manage
# the full toolchain from .tool-versions.

# Base image — lightweight Debian base; all tooling (including Go) is
# installed by mise from .tool-versions, so we don't need the golang image.
image: debian:bookworm-slim

# Bootstrap the development environment before the flow executes.
setup_script:
  # Install system dependencies required by mise and the build toolchain
  - apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl git make ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  # Install mise — the project's tool version manager
  - curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh
  - export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
  # Install all tools pinned in .tool-versions:
  #   Go 1.26.3, golangci-lint 2.12.2, shellcheck 0.11.0,
  #   markdownlint-cli2 0.22.1, vale 3.14.1, lychee 0.24.2,
  #   Node.js 24.15.0, lefthook 2.0.2
  - mise install
  - eval "$(mise activate bash)"
  # Install commitlint dependencies (validates conventional commit messages)
  - cd scripts/commit-lint && npm install && cd ../..
  # Pre-download Go module dependencies
  - go mod download
  # Activate git hooks — gives the agent automatic validation on commit/push
  - lefthook install

# Cache dependencies and tools between flow runs.
cache:
  key:
    files:
      - go.sum
      - .tool-versions
  paths:
    # Go module cache (GOPATH defaults to ~/go when installed via mise)
    - /root/go/pkg/mod/
    # mise tool installations
    - /root/.local/share/mise/
files..gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml:
# Custom review instructions for GitLab Duo Code Review.
# Spec: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/customize/review_instructions/
#
# When updating: keep rules concrete and grep-able. Reference helpers by
# their package + name (for example, `cmdutils.NewEnumValue`,
# `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest`) rather than vague guidance like "follow the
# canonical pattern". Inlined rule text is used verbatim by Duo; file
# references get summarized.
instructions:
  # ============================================================
  # GENERAL GO CODE
  # ============================================================

  - name: Error handling
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      Most basics here are enforced by `errcheck`, `errorlint`, and
      `staticcheck ST1005` in `.golangci.yml`. The rules below are the
      project-specific judgments those linters can't make.
      1. For `cmd.Flags().MarkRequired(...)` / `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive(...)`
         and similar cobra calls that return an error, use `cobra.CheckErr(err)`
         rather than `_ = ...`.
      2. When a function has a primary error and a deferred cleanup error
         (e.g., `defer file.Close()`), combine them with `errors.Join(primary, cleanupErr)`.
         Do not print one and return the other; that splits the failure across
         surfaces.
      3. For deferred cleanup that must affect the returned error, use a named
         return value and a closure:

         ```go
         func doThing() (err error) {
             f, err := os.Open(...)
             if err != nil { return err }
             defer func() { err = errors.Join(err, f.Close()) }()
             ...
         }
         ```
      4. When a function returns `(value, error)`, do not silently convert a
         sentinel error into `return nil, nil`. Distinguish "not found" from
         "real error" via an explicit sentinel (e.g., `errors.Is(err,
         ErrNotFound)`) or by documenting the contract. Quiet `(nil, nil)`
         on a sentinel hides bugs at the call site.
      5. Do not silently fall back to a default value or behavior when an
         error occurs. Surface the error (return it, or log via the
         `internal/dbg` package); let the caller choose the fallback.
         Eating the error and substituting a default is a debugging
         dead-end.

  - name: Go idioms (Go 1.26+)
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      The project is on Go 1.26+. The `modernize` linter enforces `any`,
      `slices.*`, `strings.Cut*`, and similar Go 1.21+ idioms, and `gocritic`
      (diagnostic + style tags) enforces many of the rest. The remaining
      project-specific judgments:
      1. Prefer `new(literalValue)` over `gitlab.Ptr(literalValue)` or
         intermediate variables for pointer-to-literal. For example, write
         `new(true)` rather than `gitlab.Ptr(true)`. Background: client-go 3.0
         deprecates `gitlab.Ptr`.
      2. Replace long `if / else if / else if` chains over the same value with
         a `switch` statement. Enforced by `gocritic`'s `ifElseChain`; prefer
         `switch` here over the inverted-guard style, which applies to a long
         block gated by one condition.
      3. Use `map[K]struct{}` (not `map[K]bool`) for set-membership data
         structures — less allocation, clearer intent.
      4. Prefer `iter.Seq` / `iter.Seq2` range-over-func iterators (Go 1.23+)
         for paged or generator-style traversals where they're available.
      5. Compile regular expressions once at package scope (`var fooRe = regexp.MustCompile(...)`),
         not inside the hot path of a function.

  - name: Naming
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      1. Names describe the value, not the code that produced it. If a function
         no longer needs full `iostreams.IOStreams` and only writes, rename the
         parameter to `out io.Writer`. If a parameter's role changes, rename it.
      2. When a function has a side effect (creating files, mutating state),
         the name should reflect it. Split `ConfigFile()` (read-only) from
         `EnsureConfigFile()` (creates if missing).
      3. New command sub-packages export a single constructor named `NewCmd`,
         not `NewCmdList` / `NewCmdGet` / etc. — the package name already
         carries the verb.
      4. Avoid identifier names that only differ from existing ones by suffix
         (e.g., `projectAccessTokenResponseJson` next to
         `projectAccessTokenResponse`). Pick a name that distinguishes the role.
      5. Unexport types, constants, and functions that are not used outside
         their package. Public API surface is a maintenance commitment.
      6. When introducing a helper, field, or option that parallels a
         standard-library API (especially `net/http`), mirror the stdlib
         name. Example: a helper that derives an HTTP proxy URL from
         glab's config is named `ProxyFromConfig` (parallel to
         `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`), the struct field is `proxy` (parallel
         to `http.Transport.Proxy`), the client option is `WithProxy`.
         Don't bake the protocol into a name when the field is
         protocol-agnostic (e.g., a generic proxy config key should be
         `proxy`, not `https_proxy`).

  - name: Code reuse and dead code
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      Dead code, unused fields, and unused parameters are enforced by
      `unused` and `unparam` in `.golangci.yml`. The remaining rules
      are project-specific code-reuse judgments.
      1. Before adding a new helper, search the codebase for existing equivalents.
         Common locations: `internal/cmdutils/`, `internal/iostreams/`,
         `internal/testing/cmdtest/`, `internal/api/`, `internal/glrepo/`,
         `internal/tableprinter/`, `internal/text/`. **Reuse, do not re-derive.**
      2. If a new function substantially duplicates an existing one (bulk vs.
         single-item operations, paired endpoint builders), refactor: call the
         single-item function in a loop, or extract a shared helper.
      3. Tests that don't make a meaningful assertion (e.g., construct a value
         and check `assert.NotNil`) must either be strengthened to test behavior
         or removed. `assert.True(t, true)` placeholders are not acceptable.
      4. Function signatures should accept only the values they actually use.
         If a helper only needs `note.Position`, take `*gitlab.NotePosition`,
         not `*gitlab.Note`. Avoid passing `cmdutils.Factory` into helpers —
         pass the resolved `glrepo.Interface` / `*gitlab.Client` / branch
         string directly.
      5. Prefer returning parsed/typed values (e.g., `*url.URL`, `time.Duration`)
         over strings that the caller must re-parse. The parser belongs next
         to the producer.
      6. Inline single-use, single-line helpers at the call site unless the
         helper carries a meaningful name. A two-statement helper called from
         one place is rarely worth the indirection.
      7. For ANSI-color stripping in tests, use `github.com/acarl005/stripansi`
         (already a project dep) — see `internal/commands/schedule/list/list_test.go`.
         Don't hand-roll regex stripping.

  - name: Comments
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      `scripts/comment-overlap` rejects comments whose every word is already
      carried by the adjacent code, and `gocritic`'s `commentedOutCode`
      rejects commented-out code. Do not re-flag either. Those gates are
      deliberately conservative and leave two gaps worth reviewing:
      1. Partial restatement passes the gate. A comment only has to add one
         word the code lacks to survive it, so `// Trim whitespace from the
         line first` above `line = strings.TrimSpace(line)` still ships.
         Document only what a competent Go reader cannot infer from the code,
         and delete a restating comment rather than rewording it.
      2. Godoc length is unenforced. `staticcheck` ST1020-ST1022 check the
         form of a doc comment, nothing checks whether it earns its lines,
         and doc comments are the larger share of comment volume in this
         repo. Keep godoc to what the name and signature do not convey.

      In both cases the test is whether the comment carries *why* — a
      non-obvious constraint, an ordering requirement, an upstream bug being
      worked around, a rejected alternative. Prose narrating *what* the code
      does is the common failure.

  - name: Control flow
    fileFilters:
      - '**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      1. Prefer inverted-guard / early-return style: when a long block is gated
         by a single condition, flip it to `if !cond { return ... }` so the
         happy path is unindented.
      2. Declare variables as close to their use as possible. Don't pre-declare
         at function top when only an inner block needs them.
      3. Thread `context.Context` from `cmd.Context()` through every function
         that calls into the GitLab client or another context-aware API. Pass
         it via `gitlab.WithContext(ctx)` to client-go methods. Never drop the
         context partway down the call chain.

  # ============================================================
  # COMMANDS
  # ============================================================

  - name: Command structure
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/commands/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      New (sub-)commands under `internal/commands/**` must follow the
      "Command Structure" pattern in `CONTRIBUTING.md:185-195`:

      1. Each (sub-)command is in its own package. The file where the cobra
         command is defined is named the same as the package.
      2. The command is created by a factory function named `NewCmd` (no
         package-name suffix like `NewCmdList`) that takes a single argument:
         the `cmdutils.Factory`.
      3. Define an unexported `options` struct (just `options`, not
         `xxxOptions`) inside the package. Methods and fields on `options` are
         not exported. Optional constructor named `newOptions`.
      4. In `NewCmd`, instantiate `opts := &options{...}` and pre-assign
         factory dependencies onto the struct: `io: f.IO()`,
         `baseRepo: f.BaseRepo`, `gitlabClient: f.GitLabClient`, etc.
      5. Create the cobra command in a local `cmd` variable.
      6. If multiple flags are added, retrieve `cmd.Flags()` once into a local
         `fl` variable and use `fl` for all registrations.
      7. Split logic into three methods on `*options`:
         - `complete(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error` — populate
           `opts` from CLI input.
         - `validate() error` — validate the completed options beyond what
           cobra can enforce.
         - `run(ctx context.Context) error` — execute the business logic.
         Only implement the methods you actually need.
      8. The `cobra.Command.RunE` calls `complete` → `validate` → `run` and
         passes `cmd.Context()` to `run`. **No business logic, validation, or
         API calls in `RunE` itself.**
      9. Commands must never read from or write to `os.Stdin/Stdout/Stderr`
         directly. Always go through `opts.io` (an `*iostreams.IOStreams`
         assigned from `f.IO()`).
      10. If a needed seam is missing on `cmdutils.Factory` (e.g., for
          subprocess execution), add it to the factory rather than introducing
          a package-level `var foo = func(...)` shim. The factory exists to
          provide test seams cleanly.

      Canonical reference: `internal/commands/gpg-key/get/get.go`.

  - name: Command documentation
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/commands/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      CLI documentation is generated from Go source files by `make gen-docs`.
      The following rules apply to the documentation fields of `cobra.Command`
      definitions.

      Short description (`Short` field):
      1. Write in the imperative mood. For example: `Create a new merge request.`
      2. End with a period.
      3. Do not duplicate the command name.
      4. For experimental commands, append `(EXPERIMENTAL)`.

      Synopsis (`Long` field):
      5. All new commands must include a `Long` field.
      6. Do not repeat information already in the `Short` field.
      7. Use lists for multiple constraints, input types, or behavioral differences.
      8. If the command requires a minimum GitLab version, state it.
         For example: `This command requires GitLab 17.0 or later.`
      9. **Do not reference underlying REST or GraphQL endpoint paths in
         user-facing `Long` text.** Describe what the user gets, not how it's
         implemented. Internals leak into docs and rot.
      10. Document environment variables via the `cobra.Command.Annotations`
          map (key: `help:environment`), not inside `Long`.
      11. Write each paragraph in `Long` as one source line. Cobra emits
          `Long` verbatim, so hard-wrapped source stays hard-wrapped in the
          terminal — the terminal then re-wraps around the source breaks,
          producing orphan fragments. Bullets, section headers, and
          `Example` lines are exempt.

      Usage line / positional arguments (`Use` field):
      12. Format positional arguments with these conventions:
          - Required: `<arg>` (e.g., `glab mr view <id>`).
          - Optional: `[<arg>]` (e.g., `glab ci trace [<job-id>]`).
          - One of several, required: `<id | branch | url>`
            (e.g., `glab mr checkout <id | branch | url>`).
          - One of several, optional: `[<id | branch>]`
            (e.g., `glab mr note list [<id | branch>]`).

      Experimental and beta features:
      13. Use `text.ExperimentalString` or `text.BetaString` from
          `internal/text/text.go`. Do not copy these strings manually.
      14. When only a flag is experimental, prepend `(EXPERIMENTAL)` to its
          description and add a note in `Long` explaining feature flag
          requirements.

      Examples (`Example` field):
      15. Every command must include at least one realistic example. Do not
          use examples that only repeat the command syntax.
      16. Examples live on the leaf command they apply to, not on parent
          group commands.
      17. Annotate examples with an inline comment using `# Comment text`
          above the command. Lead with the simplest realistic invocation and
          annotate even that one — explicit beats implicit for users scanning
          `--help`.
      18. For commands with many options, show the most common combinations first.
      19. Use `heredoc.Doc(\`...\`)` (from `github.com/MakeNowJust/heredoc/v2`)
          for multi-line `Long` and `Example` content. Indent with tabs (the
          heredoc package strips them). Never build these fields by
          concatenating quoted literals with embedded `\n`:
          ```go
          Long: "First line.\n\n" +
              "Second line.",
          ```
          Error and log messages are out of scope.
      20. A heredoc block is a Go raw string, so it cannot contain a backtick
          or an escape sequence — a literal `\n` renders as the two characters
          `\` and `n`. If the content needs either, use `heredoc.Docf` with
          `%[1]s` in place of each backtick and `` "`" `` as the final
          argument:
          ```go
          Long: heredoc.Docf(`
              Use %[1]s--foo%[1]s to enable foo.
          `, "`"),
          ```
          Reference: `internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_create.go`.

      Flag descriptions:
      21. Start each flag description with a capital letter and end with a period.
      22. Use angle-bracket placeholders for user-supplied values:
          `<username>`, `<branch>`, `<id>`.
      23. Do not manually annotate boolean flag defaults. pflag automatically
          appends `(default true)` for boolean flags whose default is `true`.
          Do not add it manually. No default annotation is required for boolean
          flags whose default is `false`; do not add `(default false)`.
      24. Use standard metavars for common value types: `username` for a
          username, `string` for a branch name / file path / output format,
          `int` for an integer ID.
      25. For output-format flags, use `-F, --output [text | json]` as the
          canonical form.
      26. For slice flags (`StringSliceVar`, `Int64SliceVar`, etc.), include
          the phrase: `Multiple <items> can be comma-separated or specified by
          repeating the flag.` Use `StringArrayVar` if comma-separation should
          NOT be supported.
      27. Do not use `-v` as a shorthand for anything — it collides with
          `--verbose` and `--version` conventions.

  - name: Help text sources
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      1. Do not embed help text from a sidecar `.md` file with `//go:embed`.
         Inline the content in the Go source via `heredoc.Doc`. Sidecar
         files bypass the CI markdown lint glob and split help text
         across two files without a corresponding readability win.
         `make check-embed` enforces this.

  - name: Flag handling
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/commands/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      1. Prefer cobra's built-in flag/argument helpers over manual checks:
         - `cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("a", "b")` instead of hand-rolled
           `if foo != "" && bar != "" { return error }`.
         - `cmd.MarkFlagsRequiredTogether("a", "b")`.
         - `cmd.MarkFlagsOneRequired("a", "b")` when at least one is required.
         - `cmd.MarkFlagRequired("flag")`.
         - `Args: cobra.ExactArgs(N)` / `cobra.NoArgs` / `cobra.RangeArgs(...)`
           instead of manual `len(args) != N` checks in `RunE`/`complete`.
           For commands that take no positional arguments, use `cobra.NoArgs`,
           never `cobra.ExactArgs(0)` — `NoArgs` names the unexpected argument
           in its error. Enforced by `make check-args`.
      2. For closed-set string flags, use `cmdutils.NewEnumValue(allowedValues,
         defaultValue)` from `internal/cmdutils/enum_flag.go`. Do not validate
         the string by hand in `complete`/`validate`.
      3. Use typed cobra flag variants where available: `Int64Var`, `BoolVar`,
         `TimeVar`, etc. Do not parse times/numbers from `StringVar` by hand.
      4. To target a project, use `cmdutils.EnableRepoOverride(cmd, f)` from
         `internal/cmdutils/repo_override.go` (`-R/--repo`). Do not invent a
         custom `--project` flag.
      5. For group-scoped commands, use `cmdutils.GroupOverride`.
      6. When `-R`, `--group`, and `--instance` coexist, mark them mutually
         exclusive: `cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("repo", "group", "instance")`.
      7. Required flags are often a "bad" UX choice — prefer the first
         positional argument when there's a clear primary subject (e.g., the
         token ID, the runner ID).
      8. To detect whether a flag was explicitly set by the user (vs. left
         at its default), use `cmd.Flags().Changed("<name>")`. Do not infer
         "unset" by comparing the bound value to its default — that breaks
         when the user explicitly passes the default value, and it makes the
         "no flag" case impossible to distinguish from "flag = default".

  - name: IO streams and output
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/commands/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      The rules below are the project-specific output conventions.
      1. For JSON output, use `opts.io.PrintJSON(v)` from
         `internal/iostreams/print_json.go`. `PrintJSON` handles `--jq`
         filtering and the nil-slice-to-`[]` normalization.
      2. To register the canonical `-F/--output [text | json]` flag plus
         `--jq`, use `cmdutils.EnableJSONOutput(cmd)` from
         `internal/cmdutils/output_format.go`. Do not invent a separate
         `--json` boolean.
      3. **JSON output is for machines, not humans.** Do not pretty-print or
         wrap it. Users can pipe to `jq` themselves.
      4. For table output, use `internal/tableprinter` (`NewTablePrinter()`,
         `AddRow(...)`, `String()`, `SetIsTTY(...)`).
      5. For interactive prompts, use the helpers on `IOStreams`:
         `Confirm`, `Input`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `Password`, `Multiline`,
         `Editor`, `DirectEditor`. Do not hand-roll `fmt.Scanln` confirmation
         loops. Check `io.PromptEnabled()` / `io.IsInteractive()` before
         prompting so `NO_PROMPT` and non-TTY users are respected.
      6. For terminal hyperlinks, use `io.Hyperlink(displayText, targetURL)`.

  - name: API client and pagination
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      1. For commands tied to one repo, use `f.GitLabClient()`. For multi-repo
         operations, use `f.ApiClient(host)`. Don't construct `*gitlab.Client`
         directly in command code.
      2. For unauthenticated flows (e.g., release-note fetching), use
         `api.NewClientFromConfig(host, config.NewBlankConfig(), ...)`. Do not
         drop down to `net/http` or `http.Get` for GitLab endpoints — even for
         downloads, prefer the `gitlab.Client`.
      3. Pass `gitlab.WithContext(ctx)` (from `cmd.Context()`) to every
         client-go call. This is non-optional.
      4. For paginated list endpoints, use `gitlab.ScanAndCollect` (or
         `gitlab.Scan2` iterators). Do not hand-roll `for page := 1;` loops.
         See `internal/cmdutils/cmdutils.go:92` for the canonical pattern.
      5. For HTTP status checks, use `resp.HasStatusCode(http.StatusXxx)` —
         never compare integers like `resp.StatusCode == 200`. Always use
         `http.Status*` constants over magic numbers.

  - name: Package layering
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/commands/**/*.go'
      - '!**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      1. API-shape concerns belong in an `api` (sub-)package, not in command
         packages or `utils` packages. GraphQL queries, REST endpoint
         construction, response struct definitions, case normalization for API
         enums — these go in `internal/api/` or a command-local `api/`
         subpackage.
      2. Command packages should focus on CLI surface: flag parsing, prompts,
         output formatting, calling into the api layer.
      3. Do not import one command package from another. Shared command-level
         utilities go in `internal/cmdutils/` (or a new shared package), not
         a sibling command.
      4. Helpers that take `io *iostreams.IOStreams` should put it as the first
         parameter to mirror the standard-library convention of `io.Writer`-
         first.

  - name: Config and environment
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      1. New configuration keys (global or per-host) are declared in
         `KeySchema` in `internal/config/schema.go` as a `KeyDef` entry.
         The schema drives the blank config, `config set` validation,
         defaults, env-var resolution, legacy aliases, and keyring
         eligibility — do not read settings ad-hoc from disk or env.
      2. Set `KeyDef.EnvVars` to declare environment variables that
         override a key (the uppercase form of the key name is the
         default when EnvVars is empty). Do not call `os.LookupEnv` /
         `os.Getenv` in command code for settings that have, or should
         have, a config-file equivalent.
      3. Document environment variables on the `cobra.Command.Annotations`
         map (key: `help:environment`), not in free-form `Long` text — that
         placement is also surfaced in generated docs.

  - name: Deprecations
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*.go'
    instructions: |
      1. When deprecating a flag with `cmd.Flags().MarkDeprecated(...)`, write
         the message as a sentence continuation: Cobra prepends
         `Flag --<flag> has been deprecated, ` (ending in a comma), so start
         your message with a lowercase letter and end with a period. For
         example, `use --output instead.` renders as
         `Flag --output-format has been deprecated, use --output instead.`.
      2. When the deprecated flag has a direct replacement, end the message
         with `use --<replacement> instead.`. When there is no replacement,
         describe the resulting behavior. For example, `tracking is enabled by default.`.
      3. Avoid time-relative words like `now` or `currently` in deprecation
         messages.
      4. When deprecating an environment variable, update the `help:environment`
         annotation in `root.go`: remove the deprecated entry, add the
         replacement with a full description, keep all entries in alphabetical
         order, and mirror the change in the README's environment variables
         section.

  # ============================================================
  # TESTS
  # ============================================================

  - name: Test setup
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      1. Use `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest(t, NewCmd, parseFlags, opts...)` from
         `internal/testing/cmdtest/factory.go` to set up command tests. It
         returns a `CmdExecFunc` you can call with the command's args.
      2. Configure test state with `FactoryOption`s — see
         `internal/testing/cmdtest/factory.go` for the full list:
         `WithStdin`, `WithBranch`, `WithBaseRepo`, `WithGitLabClient`,
         `WithApiClient`, `WithBuildInfo`, `WithExecutor`, `WithGitRunner`,
         `WithConsole`, etc.
      3. **If you need a seam that isn't there, add a new `FactoryOption` to
         `cmdtest`** — do not hand-roll factory wiring inline in the test, and
         do not introduce a package-level `var xxx = func(...)` shim in
         production code to be overridden by the test.
      4. For GitLab API mocking, use the client-go testing package:
         `gitlabtesting "gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3/testing"`.

         ```go
         tc := gitlabtesting.NewTestClient(t)
         tc.MockUsers.EXPECT().GetGPGKey(int64(123)).Return(testKey, nil, nil)
         exec := cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest(t, NewCmd, false, cmdtest.WithGitLabClient(tc.Client))
         ```

         **Do not introduce new `httpmock`-based HTTP responders** for code
         paths that go through client-go. Migrate existing HTTP mocks when
         touching files in the same package.
      5. For mock call ordering, use `gomock.InOrder(...)`.
      6. Canonical reference: `internal/commands/gpg-key/get/get_test.go`;
         JSON-assertion pattern: `internal/commands/runnercontroller/token/list/list_test.go`.

  - name: Test discipline
    fileFilters:
      - 'internal/**/*_test.go'
    instructions: |
      Many test discipline basics are enforced by linters in `.golangci.yml`:
      `testifylint` (use testify, `require` before indexing, `assert.Empty`
      over `assert.Equal(t, "", ...)`, no `require` in HTTP handlers),
      `tparallel` (`t.Parallel`), `usetesting` (`t.TempDir` / `t.Chdir` /
      `t.Setenv`). The rules below are the project-specific judgments those
      linters can't make.
      1. New behavior gated by a flag, argument shape, or branch must include
         a test for each meaningful path — including the "no flag set",
         "invalid input", and "default" branches. A new `--<flag>` must not
         ship without an exercising test.
      2. When asserting on a command's JSON output, `json.Unmarshal` into a
         typed struct and assert on fields. Do not substring-match on the raw
         JSON text (`assert.Contains(out, '"id": 1')`). Reference:
         `internal/commands/runnercontroller/token/list/list_test.go`.
      3. **Test the user-visible behavior of the command**, not the
         configuration plumbing or internal field assignments. If a test
         constructs `options{}` directly and checks a field, it probably
         should drive the command through `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` instead.
      4. Prefer flat per-case assertions over loops. `for _, tc := range
         testCases { tc.run() }` is fine for table-driven tests with shared
         setup, but don't loop over a slice just to assert each element —
         spell out the asserts (`assert.Equal(t, tokens[0].ID, results[0].ID)`,
         `assert.Equal(t, tokens[1].ID, results[1].ID)`) so failures point at
         the specific element.
      5. When adding a flag-aware test variant, keep the original no-flag
         test as well. Do not rename / repurpose existing baseline tests —
         that quietly removes coverage. Add new tests alongside, don't
         replace.
      6. When adding behavior to one of a set of parallel sibling commands
         (e.g., `token list` for project / group / personal tokens), add
         the equivalent test in each sibling package — otherwise coverage
         drifts asymmetrically.
      7. `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` produces non-TTY IOStreams by default.
         Don't reach for `t.Setenv("NO_COLOR", ...)` or other TTY-affecting
         env hacks — if you need different behavior, pass a `FactoryOption`
         (`cmdtest.WithIOStreamsOverride` or similar) rather than mutating
         process environment.
      8. Prefer test-local fixtures over package-level `var` blocks unless
         the fixture is genuinely shared by multiple tests. Local fixtures
         make ownership and lifetime obvious.

  # ============================================================
  # SHELL SCRIPTS
  # ============================================================

  - name: Shell scripts
    fileFilters:
      - 'scripts/**/*.sh'
      - '*.sh'
    instructions: |
      1. Write usage messages and error output to stderr: `echo "..." >&2`.
         User-consumable program output goes to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr.
      2. Use a direct shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env bash` or `#!/bin/sh`) and make
         the script executable. Do not invoke scripts with `bash ./script.sh`
         from other scripts or CI config — call the script directly.
      3. Validate required environment variables explicitly at the top of the
         script (e.g., `: "${APPSTORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_FILE:?must be set}"`).
         A surprising `:` mount or missing var should error early, not silently.
      4. Use `set -euo pipefail` for new scripts.

  # ============================================================
  # PROJECT-LEVEL / DEPENDENCIES
  # ============================================================

  - name: Dependencies
    fileFilters:
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'
    instructions: |
      1. Before adding a new third-party dependency, check whether the
         standard library or an existing dependency covers the need. For
         example, prefer `os.UserConfigDir` over `github.com/adrg/xdg`.
      2. New dependencies must be justified in the MR description: what the
         stdlib can't do and why an existing dep won't suffice.
      3. Unexpected `go.mod` / `go.sum` changes that don't trace to a
         deliberate need should be removed or explained.

  - name: Tool versions
    fileFilters:
      - '.tool-versions'
      - 'Makefile'
    instructions: |
      1. The project pins developer tools via `mise` and `.tool-versions`.
         When bumping a tool version (e.g., golangci-lint, Go), update both
         `.tool-versions` AND any hard-coded version in `Makefile` so local
         and CI environments stay aligned.
      2. New developer tools should be added to `.tool-versions` (not to the
         Makefile alone).

# glab CLI agent instructions

Go-based GitLab CLI. Entrypoint: `cmd/glab/main.go`. Commands live under
`internal/commands/<noun>/<verb>/` (noun-first grammar, for example,
`glab mr create`).

## Common tasks

For each common task, the one non-discoverable pointer the agent can't
infer from reading the tree.

- **Adding or editing a command** — first read the matching block of
  [`.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml`](.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml).
  It is the canonical source for code conventions (command structure,
  flag handling, IO streams, API client and pagination, test setup,
  test discipline) and is what GitLab Duo Code Review grades MRs
  against. Blocks are scoped by `fileFilters`, so only the ones that
  match the file you are editing apply.
- **Writing a comment** — default to not writing one. Document only what a
  competent Go reader cannot infer from the code; a comment that restates
  the line below it is noise, and rewording it does not help. Two gates run
  in lefthook pre-commit and the `lint:comments` CI job:
  `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap` rejects comments whose words are already
  carried by the adjacent code, and `gocritic`'s `commentedOutCode` rejects
  commented-out code. `go run ./scripts/comment-ratio -base origin/main`
  reports comment volume on a change and is advisory. Godoc on exported
  symbols is exempt from the overlap gate by position, so it is not flagged
  for repeating its own symbol name. Full rules: the `Comments` block of
  [`.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml`](.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml).
- **Looking for a helper before writing a new one** — the most common
  feedback on this project is "use the existing helper":
  - `internal/cmdutils/` — flag wiring (`EnableRepoOverride`,
    `EnableJSONOutput`, `NewEnumValue`), the `Factory` interface.
  - `internal/testing/cmdtest/` — test setup (`SetupCmdForTest`,
    `NewTestFactory`, `WithStdin`/`WithBranch`/`WithGitLabClient`).
  - `internal/iostreams/` — all output (`LogInfo*`, `LogError*`,
    `PrintJSON`) and interactive prompts (`Confirm`, `Input`, `Select`).
  - `internal/glrepo/` — repository interface.
  - `internal/tableprinter/` — formatted text output.
  - `internal/text/` — `ExperimentalString`, `BetaString`.
  - `internal/config/schema.go` — every configuration key is registered
    in `KeySchema`. Add a `KeyDef` entry to introduce a new key (it
    drives the blank config, `config set` validation, defaults, env-var
    resolution, legacy aliases, and keyring eligibility).
- **Copying from a canonical example**:
  - New command: `internal/commands/gpg-key/get/get.go`.
  - Paginated list command: `internal/commands/securefile/list/list.go`.
  - Command tests with API mocks:
    `internal/commands/gpg-key/get/get_test.go`.
  - JSON output assertion test:
    `internal/commands/runnercontroller/token/list/list_test.go`.
- **Updating a command's docs** — author the change in the Go source
  (`Short`, `Long`, `Example`, flag descriptions on the `cobra.Command`),
  run `make gen-docs`, commit the regenerated files under `docs/source/`
  in the same commit. Never edit `docs/source/` directly. `make gen-docs`
  also prunes pages for removed, deprecated, and hidden commands (and
  deletes any emptied directories), so never hand-delete pages under
  `docs/source/`. Instead regenerate the docs and commit the deletions.
- **Reviewing MR feedback** — use the `glab` CLI (or `glab` MCP tools)
  end-to-end, not raw `glab api`:
  - Fetch: `glab mr view <id> --output json`.
  - Reply: `glab mr note create --reply <discussion-id> --message "..."`.
  - Resolve: `glab mr note resolve <discussion-id>`. Pass **only** the
    discussion ID — a trailing MR ID argument errors out.
  - Add a new inline diff comment:
    `glab mr note create --file <path> --line <N>` (or `--line N:M`, or
    `--old-line N` for a deletion).
- **Creating an MR that references an issue** — add
  `/copy_metadata #<issue-id>` on its own line in the description.
  GitLab copies the issue's labels and milestone, so the
  `glab mr create --label` flags aren't needed.
- **Naming a new command or writing a commit message** — verbs follow
  noun-first grammar (`create`, `list`, `get`, `update`, `delete`);
  see `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Grammar" before introducing a new verb.
  Commit messages are Conventional Commits, enforced by the
  `commit-msg` hook through `scripts/commit-lint` (needs Node.js).

## Verify changes before you push

Lefthook runs automatically on `git push`. Install it once with
`lefthook install`. Install all tools with `make bootstrap`, which uses
`mise` and `.tool-versions`.

```shell
lefthook run pre-push  # build, lint against origin/main, test-changed, generated-doc/code check, markdown/vale/lychee
make check             # test + lint
```

To skip hooks, use `LEFTHOOK=0 git push` or
`LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=pre-push git push`. Treat these like `--no-verify`, an
escape hatch for debugging the hooks themselves, not a workaround for slow
builds. The hooks catch generated-doc/code drift and lint regressions
before merge.

## Common commands

```shell
make build                                    # compile to ./bin/glab
make lint                                     # golangci-lint (full)
make fix                                      # golangci-lint --fix + gofmt + goimports
make test                                     # all unit tests (gotestsum, writes coverage.txt/xml)
make test-changed                             # tests changed packages + reverse deps against origin/main
make test-race                                # unit tests with -race
go test ./internal/commands/mr/note/...       # single package
go test ./internal/commands/mr/note/... -run TestCreate
make gen-docs                                 # regenerate docs/source/** from cobra definitions
make generate                                 # go generate ./... (includes config stubs)
make gen-config                               # config stubs from internal/config/config.yaml.lock
```

`make test` forcibly clears `VISUAL`, `EDITOR`, `PAGER`, and `GITLAB_TOKEN`,
and sets `CI_PROJECT_PATH` from the origin remote. Some tests depend on
this. If you run `go test` directly and see environment-dependent failures,
replicate that setup.

> [!note]
> Local vendor workflow: `vendor/` is gitignored. Do not request vendor
> updates in merge requests. On an inconsistent-vendoring error,
> run `go mod vendor` to resync. Do not use `-mod=mod`, which bypasses the
> vendor directory instead of fixing it.

## Integration tests

Integration tests are tagged `//go:build integration`, use the file suffix
`_integration_test.go`, and use the test name suffix `_Integration`. They
are not run by `make test`. To run them, use `make integration-test-race`,
which adds `-tags=integration`. They call a real GitLab instance. Locally
they are skipped unless both `GITLAB_TEST_HOST` and `GITLAB_TOKEN_TEST` are
set (see `GetHostOrSkip` in `test/helpers.go`). The token must have the
`api` scope. The
`glab duo` tests require a GitLab Duo-enabled user.

## Environment variables

- `GITLAB_TOKEN` — API token. Overrides configuration.
- `GITLAB_HOST`, `GITLAB_URI`, `GL_HOST` — Default GitLab instance,
  outside Git repositories.
- `GLAB_CONFIG_DIR` — Overrides the configuration directory. Highest priority.
- `GLAB_ENABLE_CI_AUTOLOGIN=true` — Together with `GITLAB_CI=true`,
  enables `CI_JOB_TOKEN` auto-login.
- `GLAB_DEBUG=true` — Verbose logging for Git commands, expanded aliases, and
  DNS.
